chunks: And from him, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abā al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a sick man who arrives in Makkah and is unable to perform tawaf around the House, nor the sa'y between al-Safa and al-Marwah.

He said: He should be carried and taken around, trailing the ground with his feet, until his feet touch the ground during the tawaf. Then he should be made to stand at the base of al-Safa and al-Marwah if he is ill.

key_terms.الصَّفَا: al-Safa, one of the two points of sa'y
key_terms.الْمَرِيضِ: the sick person whose physical condition prevents independent ritual performance
key_terms.الْمَرْوَةِ: al-Marwah, the other point of sa'y
key_terms.بِالْبَيْتِ: around the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.مَحْمُولًا: while being carried due to inability to move independently
key_terms.يَطُوفَ: to perform tawaf around the Ka'bah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a sick person who cannot perform tawaf and sa'y in Makkah?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a sick person who reaches Makkah but cannot perform tawaf or sa'y independently. It instructs that he be carried during tawaf with his feet touching the ground, and then be positioned at al-Safa and al-Marwah when illness prevents normal performance.
